questions.stem: What central structure does the Unified Star Schema (USS) introduce?
options: The Puppini Bridge
The Hub table
The Anchor table
The Descriptor table
The Satellite table
questions.explanation: USS enhances traditional star schemas by introducing a central structure known as the Puppini Bridge, which aligns facts and dimensions into a single analytical framework.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of the Unified Star Schema?
options: Normalising dimensions to 3NF
Providing a unified query entry point that eliminates ambiguity when working with multiple fact tables
Storing every attribute on its own timeline
Replacing dimensions with knots
Reducing the fact table to a single row per customer
questions.explanation: USS gives analysts a single entry point so that drill-across analysis is simpler and results are consistent without deep SQL expertise.

A relationship between facts and dimensions that is ambiguous or missing
A join that multiplies rows incorrectly
A bridge with too many sparse keys
A dimension that changes too slowly
questions.explanation: Fan traps occur when joins multiply rows incorrectly; chasm traps occur when relationships between facts and dimensions are ambiguous or missing.

questions.stem: What does the Puppini Bridge essentially consist of?
options: A pre-aggregated summary of all measures
A normalised copy of every dimension
A list of slowly changing attribute versions
A union of keys from all relevant facts and dimensions
A hierarchy of parent–child pointers
questions.explanation: The bridge acts as a "superstar" table that is essentially a union of keys from all relevant facts and dimensions.

questions.stem: How do analysts query a Unified Star Schema?
options: They start from each fact table and inner-join to the bridge
They start from the largest dimension
They query the fact tables directly and union the results
They traverse edges from a customer node
They begin at the bridge and left-join to any required fact or dimension
questions.explanation: Instead of starting from individual fact tables, analysts begin at the bridge and left-join to required facts or dimensions, preventing incorrect aggregations and row multiplication.

questions.stem: Which combined report is given as an example that a Puppini Bridge makes safe in a loan approval environment?
options: Approval-to-Repayment Conversion by Customer Segment
Which customers share the same contact details
What rate was valid as of 20 January 2024
Which loan documents embed officer O11
Which events rebuild loan L001
questions.explanation: With the bridge in place analysts can safely produce cross-fact reports such as Approval-to-Repayment Conversion by Customer Segment or Default Rates by Officer Branch and Product Type.

questions.stem: Why does the Unified Star Schema support self-service BI well?
options: Because it removes all dimensions
Because queries always originate from a unified structure, so business users can explore multiple processes without deep warehouse knowledge
Because it stores data as JSON
Because it requires no joins at all
Because it pre-computes every possible report
questions.explanation: Because queries always start from the bridge, business users can explore data across multiple processes without knowing warehouse internals, and new facts can be added without breaking reports.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a trade-off of the Unified Star Schema?
options: The bridge can become wide and sparse with many unpopulated keys
Careful storage and indexing strategies are required
New fact tables cannot be added without breaking existing reports
Strong governance over conformed dimensions and keys is essential
Some measures may need restructuring, which can feel counterintuitive to fact-centric modellers
questions.explanation: The ability to add new fact tables later without breaking existing reports is a strength of USS, not a trade-off.

questions.stem: To which modelling family does the Unified Star Schema belong?
options: The ensemble family
The pre-relational family
The NoSQL family
Primarily the Dimensional Modelling domain, as a dimensional–semantic hybrid
The temporal family
questions.explanation: USS belongs primarily to Dimensional Modelling but can be considered a dimensional–semantic hybrid focused on analytical clarity rather than normalisation theory.

questions.stem: Why does the query logic built on the Bridge_Puppini remain valid when new facts such as Repayments or Collections are added later?
options: Because the facts are merged into one table
Because the dimensions are re-normalised
Because every fact is stored in the bridge as a measure
Because the bridge is rebuilt from scratch each time
Because the bridge is the single entry point for all queries
questions.explanation: Because the bridge is the single entry point, existing logic that pulls customer, officer, date and status details stays valid even when new fact tables are added.
